question: In human female, when egg is not fertilised, which of the following process takes place?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Menstruation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Menstruation** refers to the periodic shedding of the uterine lining (endometrium) in human females when fertilization of the egg does not occur.
 
• This process is part of the **menstrual cycle**, which typically lasts around **28 days**, though it can range from 21 to 35 days in different individuals.
 
• Menstruation occurs due to a drop in the levels of the hormones **estrogen** and **progesterone**, leading to the breakdown and discharge of the endometrial lining.
 
• The **discharge** during menstruation consists of blood, mucus, and tissue from the uterine lining, and it typically lasts for **3-7 days**.
 
• It is a natural and essential part of the female reproductive cycle, preparing the body for a potential pregnancy each month. If fertilization does not occur, the uterine lining is shed, and the cycle begins again.
